results.evidence: Real contradiction: gain_ft 6120 and loss_ft 9500 differ on an out-and-back, and the itinerary sums to 7000/7000. 6120 equals the bare elevation range (2,080 to 8,200 ft) published for the trip, not a cumulative gain. results.evidence: The peak's standard description states there are two 8,200+ closed contours and the easterly of the two is highest by 10-15 ft, both above an 8,197 ft benchmarked crag further east. Waypoint/beta/pitch_detail/baseFinding/day-2 objective rewritten to agree with the itinerary schedule, which already had it right; pin coordinates untouched, so the waypoint is renamed neutrally.

results.fact: Total elevation gain for the route
results.evidence: Real: gain_ft 1500 cannot be a car-to-car total, since the trailhead (~3,660 ft) to summit (7,762 ft) net rise alone is ~4,100 ft. But the itinerary's '~9,000+ ft' for Day 1 alone is also doubtful: published segments give ~1,700 ft trailhead to Cascade Pass, Cache Col at ~6,900 ft, and ~2,000 ft from Kool-Aid Lake to Yang Yang Lakes (roughly 5,000 ft to camp), and a whole 30-mile north-to-south traverse is quoted at ~11,000 ft. No source giving a car-to-car gain for Le Conte was found, so no value is written; both gain_ft and the Day 1 '~9,000+ ft' need a sourced total.
